hero.h1: Kitchen Remodeling in Santa Cruz, From Design to Final Walkthrough
hero.subheadline: Elite Construction pairs in-house interior designers with its own lead carpenters, so your kitchen, bath or ADU is planned and built by one team. Owners Eric Lamascus and Craig Yates have remodeled Santa Cruz County homes for more than two decades.

image.alt: Kitchen remodeling Santa Cruz project with a black and white geometric tile backsplash, white custom range hood, brass drum light and black-framed windows

intro.h2: An engineer and a Kiwi carpenter, building in Santa Cruz
paragraphs: Elite Construction has provided kitchen remodeling in Santa Cruz County for more than twenty years, along with bath renovations, additions and ADUs. The firm works from 347 Soquel Ave in Santa Cruz and knows the coastal conditions, permit processes and neighborhood styles from Aptos to Scotts Valley.

The partnership began on a rugby field. Eric Lamascus was an engineer in high-tech automation, and Craig Yates had finished a four-year building apprenticeship in his native New Zealand. They set out to make remodeling less stressful and more transparent, which shows in bids that break out labor, materials and subcontractors, plus an online portal for every job.

services.h2: Kitchen remodeling in Santa Cruz, plus baths, whole homes and ADUs

items.name: Kitchens
items.blurb: Smart layouts and standout finishes, from a navy and walnut kitchen to a Pleasure Point remodel and a custom kitchen in the Santa Cruz Mountains. 'Better' kitchens add soft-close drawers, quartz or granite tops and upgraded fixtures. 'Best' brings custom cabinetry and can move walls or plumbing.

image.alt: Santa Cruz Mountains kitchen with a hammered copper apron sink, knotty alder cabinets, open shelves and a wide window onto the trees

items.name: Bathrooms
items.blurb: Relaxed, refined bathroom remodels with curbless showers, soaking tubs, Fireclay tile and custom vanities. Recent work includes a Pleasure Point bath with ocean views, a Pasatiempo update that traded a tub for a curbless walk-in shower, and a rustic primary bath with a hammered metal double sink.

image.alt: Pasatiempo bathroom remodel with a wood double vanity, black hex tile floor and curbless walk-in shower with a black granite bench

items.name: Whole Home Remodels
items.blurb: Transformational work across a whole house or condo, such as a coastal condo remodel in Santa Cruz and a Santa Cruz Mountains hideaway with a steel-clad fireplace. Each job runs on an online portal that tracks material deadlines, install dates and a running total of costs.

image.alt: Santa Cruz Mountains home remodel with a riveted steel fireplace surround, arched firebox door and reclaimed wood mantel

items.name: ADUs and Additions
items.blurb: Detached ADUs and additions built for Santa Cruz County lots. One rustic detached ADU in Santa Cruz has reclaimed wood siding, a pitched metal roof and French doors. A permit and estimate coordinator on staff keeps the paperwork moving while the design is finished.

image.alt: Rustic detached ADU in Santa Cruz with reclaimed wood siding, a pitched metal roof and French doors under oak trees

about.h2: Eric Lamascus and Craig Yates, partners since the rugby field
about.text: Eric Lamascus and Craig Yates met playing rugby. Eric, now CEO, was a former engineer from Oklahoma working in high-tech automation. Craig had just finished a demanding four-year building apprenticeship in New Zealand, where construction standards are high. They formed Elite to make remodeling less stressful and more transparent, and they stay selective about the projects they take on. Today the owners lead a team of designers, coordinators, project managers and carpenters. Their own tagline sums up the goal: proof that you can love your contractor.

image.alt: Headshots of Eric Lamascus and Craig Yates, owners of Elite Construction in Santa Cruz, CA

process.h2: How an Elite remodel moves, step by step

steps.title: Share your ideas
steps.text: Call or email with photos and Pinterest or Houzz boards so the team can give a ballpark cost and judge whether it is a good fit.

steps.title: Design consultation at home
steps.text: A designer visits to learn your taste, wishes and budget so the bid that follows is accurate.

steps.title: Line-by-line estimate review
steps.text: You go through the bid line by line, with design and construction options to fit the scope to your budget.

steps.title: Finalize the design
steps.text: After pricing appliances and fixtures, you lock the layout. The online portal then shows material deadlines, install dates and running costs.

steps.title: Build, then relax
steps.text: Crews build the project and keep you in the loop. If an issue comes up after you move back in, the Elite guarantee covers you.

service_area.h2: Where Elite works in Santa Cruz County
service_area.text: Elite serves Santa Cruz County from its office in the Soquel Ocean Center at 347 Soquel Ave. The footer names Aptos, Soquel, Capitola, Santa Cruz and Scotts Valley, and finished projects sit in Pleasure Point, Pasatiempo, Seabright, Midtown and the Santa Cruz Mountains. Clients quoted on the site also live in Ben Lomond. Twenty-plus years here means the team knows coastal conditions and local permit processes.

faq.h2: What Santa Cruz homeowners ask Elite

items.q: How much does a kitchen remodel cost in Santa Cruz?
items.a: Elite's pricing page lists a standard kitchen at $55,000 and up at its 'Better' level and $65,000 and up at 'Best.' Large kitchens start around $65,000 for 'Better' and $100,000 for 'Best.' Elite does not take 'Economy' work, which it describes as a typical rental-property remodel.

items.q: What does a bathroom remodel cost?
items.a: A medium bathroom starts around $25,000 at the 'Better' level and $35,000 at 'Best.' A large bathroom starts around $35,000 for 'Better' and $60,000 for 'Best.' 'Better' covers quartz or granite tops and upgraded fixtures, while 'Best' adds custom cabinetry, designer fixtures and possible plumbing moves.

Yes. Elite offers a free, no-obligation preliminary estimate for any project you are considering. Sending photos of your space and your Pinterest or Houzz boards helps the team give you a ballpark cost early, so you can decide whether Elite is a good fit before the design visit.

items.q: How will I know where my project and budget stand?
items.a: Each client gets access to an online portal. It shows detailed timelines for the materials you need to choose, such as tile and fixtures, the install dates for every phase, and a running total of expenses. Reviewers also praise steady communication from the bid through the build.

Yes. Elite builds ADUs and additions as well as kitchens, baths and whole-home remodels. Its gallery includes a rustic detached ADU in Santa Cruz with reclaimed wood siding, a pitched metal roof and French doors. A permit and estimate coordinator on staff helps keep the approvals on track.

final_cta.text: Call (831) 234-5052 or email Eric at EL@DiscoverElite.com for a free, no-obligation preliminary estimate.
